fact_types.title: The child meets the relationship test to be your qualifying child for the earned income credit: son, daughter, stepchild, eligible foster child, or a descendant of any of them; brother, sister, half brother, half sister, stepbrother, stepsister, or a descendant of any of them. Yes means the child meets the test. No means the child does not qualify. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession.

The child meets the age test for the earned income credit: at the end of 2025 was under age 19 and younger than you (or your spouse if filing jointly), or was under age 24, a full-time student, and younger than you (or your spouse if filing jointly), or was any age and permanently and totally disabled. Yes means the child meets the test. No means the child does not qualify. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession.

The child lived with you in the United States for more than half of 2025, taking into account temporary absences, birth or death during 2025, or extended active-duty military service. Yes means the child meets the residency test. No means the child does not qualify. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession.

The child was not married at the end of 2025, or you can claim the child as a dependent, and the child did not file a joint return for 2025 (or filed only to claim a refund of withheld income tax or estimated tax paid). Yes means the child meets the joint-return test. No means the child does not qualify. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession.

The child has a social security number issued by the Social Security Administration on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions) that is valid for the earned income credit. Yes means the child has a valid SSN. No means the child cannot be counted in figuring the credit with qualifying children. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession.

Another person may also claim this child as a qualifying child for the earned income credit for 2025 under the tie-breaker rules. Yes is outside the supported class and blocks. No means no other person may claim the child. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession.

Answered on a married filing separately or head of household return with a qualifying child. Yes if you were not married at the end of 2025; or, if married, you did not share a principal residence with your spouse for the last 6 months of 2025, or you were legally separated under state law under a written separation agreement or decree of separate maintenance and lived apart from your spouse at the end of 2025. No means you were married and neither applies, so the credit is $0 (2025 Form 1040 instructions, line 27a Step 3 questions 3-5). Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession.
